headline: Process EXEC, not codegen, dominates a cold `go build`.
sizing: A cold `go build` of a one-file main spawns ~61 tool processes (27 compile, 34 asm, link, go). At ~129 ms of carrick exec cost each, exec accounts for roughly 8 s of the ~10.4 s build - about 76%. Docker pays ~1.05 ms per exec, so essentially all of that 8 s is carrick overhead.
phase_note: Measured with carrick's own `dsr-cache-lifecycle` USDT probes under `dtrace -Z` (20 execs of the 20 MB `compile` binary). The prepared-image path IS taken - no ineligibility is logged - so the child does not re-read the ELF. The remainder is the parent's full-file read and SHA-256, address-space setup, and translating the Go runtime's startup path.
sha256: On an exec-heavy workload `sha2::sha256::compress256` is 6.99% of ALL CPU and 44% of carrick's own userspace - the per-exec full-file digest at `native_darwin.rs:947`. The same binary is hashed on every one of the 61 execs.
io: 685 MB of `pread` and 2.34 GB of `read` per build, measured at the syscall provider. 61 execs x (one ~20 MB ELF read + one ~20 MB prepared-artifact build) accounts for it.
shared_translation_on_this_workload: 3.3% (2498 ms vs 2582 ms median over 20 execs). The lane fixed today helps, but it is not the dominant term.
consequence: The campaign has been ranking against steady-state emitted code, which is ~45% of build CPU. That is the right target for long-running guests, but for a BUILD - many short processes - the per-exec startup cost dominates, and the same executable pays it 61 times. The lever is a container-lifetime cache of per-executable exec work (digest + prepared image), keyed like the shared-translation store: pay once for `compile`, not 27 times.
caveats: Wall figures are from an untraced run; the phase split is from a probe-instrumented run and is proportional, not wall evidence. `/bin/true` isolates the size-independent floor (19 ms); the 20 MB binary shows the size-dependent part.
